source.title: Polynomial point counts and odd cohomology vanishing on moduli spaces of stable curves
source.authors: Jonas Bergström, Carel Faber and Sam Payne
source.version: arXiv v2 (17 October 2023, 31 pages; 'minor revisions, to appear in Ann. Math.', posted after the 27 September 2023 acceptance), read completely. The Annals article is not openly available and was not collated.
readSections: 2026-09-29: arXiv:2206.07759v2, all 31 pages: §§1–11 and references; page images checked at every source issue. The tables were recomputed with sympy: Theorems 1.4, 1.5 and 11.1 against Proposition 9.6 and §11.3, and the n = 0, 1, 2 assemblies of §10 from Propositions 5.1, 8.1–8.7.

summary: Bergström, Faber and Payne prove that H^k(M̄_{g,n}; Q) vanishes for all odd k ≤ 9, answering Arbarello and Cornalba. The induction of Arbarello–Cornalba, sharpened by the vanishing of H^{vcd}(M_g), reduces this to H⁹(M̄_{4,n}) = 0 for n ≤ 3. They get that by showing M̄_{4,n} has polynomial point count: they count genus 4 curves over F_q, the hyperelliptic ones directly and the others as (2, 3) complete intersections on the three types of quadric. A Hasse–Weil sieve built on inverse zeta functions controls the singular members, the Getzler–Kapranov formula gives the boundary, and van den Bogaart–Edixhoven turns approximate counts into cohomology. The paper also gives S_n-equivariant counts and Euler characteristics of symplectic local systems on M₄. Everything specific to moduli of curves joins the pending roadmap MotivicStructuresInModuliOfCurves proposed by Canning–Larson–Payne. The general point-counting tools are sources for WeilConjectures, the weight spectral sequence for DWP.8, and the finite-field lemmas and quadric classification for FF.1/FF.3 and GN.2.

items.name: The quadratic character of F_q
items.statement: For odd q, χ : F_q → {0, ±1} with χ(0) = 0, χ(a) = 1 for a nonzero square and −1 otherwise; Σ_{a ∈ F_q} χ(a) = 0.

items.name: Order of GL_n(F_q)
items.statement: #GL_n(F_q) = ∏_{i=0}^{n−1} (q^n − q^i); in particular #GL_2(F_q) = (q² − 1)(q² − q), and #PGL_n(F_q) = #GL_n(F_q)/(q − 1).
items.note: Mathlib gives the GL_n count; the PGL_n quotient by the scalars F_q^× is a one-line consequence.

items.name: Grothendieck–Lefschetz trace formula for varieties
items.statement: For a separated finite-type X over F_q and ℓ ∤ q, #X(F_q) = Σ_i (−1)^i Tr(F_q | H^i_{c,ét}(X_{F̄_q}, Q_ℓ)), with F_q the geometric Frobenius.
items.note: As in PAPER-SCHMIDT-STIX-16 and PAPER-LIU-WOOD-ZUREICKBROWN-24. The atlas stages import it from the upstream Cohomological Point Counting roadmap (TraceFormula Layer 8), which WC.0/WC.1 reconcile. The stack case is item prop-1-3-iv.

items.name: Hasse–Weil zeta function
items.statement: For a variety Y over F_q, Z(Y; t) := exp(Σ_{m ≥ 1} #Y(F_{q^m}) t^m / m).

items.name: Cohomological formula for the zeta function, (11)
items.statement: 1/Z(Y; t) = det(1 − t F_q | H^even_{c,ét}(Y_{F̄_q}, Q_ℓ)) / det(1 − t F_q | H^odd_{c,ét}(Y_{F̄_q}, Q_ℓ)).
items.note: WC.1 consumes the Euler product and determinant formula from the trace formula.

items.name: Zeta functions of disjoint unions and point removal, (9)–(10)
items.statement: Z(∅; t) = 1; 1/Z(Y; t) = 1/Z(Y₁; t) · 1/Z(Y₂; t) for Y = Y₁ ⊔ Y₂; hence 1/Z(Y ∖ y; t) = (1 − t)^{−1} · 1/Z(Y; t) for a rational point y.
items.note: WC.1: 'disjoint-union products, open–closed factorization'.

items.name: Étale-to-singular comparison for smooth proper families
items.statement: For X smooth and proper over Z (or Z_p) and ℓ ≠ p: H^i_ét(X_{Q̄}, Q_ℓ) ≅ H^i_ét(X_{F̄_p}, Q_ℓ) (smooth and proper base change) and dim H^i_ét(X_{Q̄}, Q_ℓ) = dim H^i(X_C, Q).
items.locator: arXiv:2206.07759v2, §1, p. 2; proof of Proposition 3.1, p. 6
items.note: WC.4 plans the Betti-number comparison in smooth proper families for schemes; the DM-stack case the paper needs is part of item vdbe-theorem-2-1.

items.name: Deligne's purity for smooth proper varieties over F_q
items.statement: Eigenvalues of F_q on H^i_ét(X_{F̄_q}, Q_ℓ) for X smooth proper over F_q are algebraic integers all of whose conjugates have absolute value q^{i/2}.
items.locator: arXiv:2206.07759v2, implicit in §1, p. 2, and Proposition 3.1, p. 6
items.note: WC.3 covers only the projective case (DWP.4). The integrated nodes WeilConjectures:WC.6/purity-for-proper-smooth-varieties and DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.7/hodge-type-triangles-and-proper-smooth-purity-3-3-7-3-3-11 plan Weil II 3.3.9 and 3.3.11 (RT-PAPER-BERGSTROM-FABER-PAYNE-24/5). The DM-stack case is deligne-purity-dm.

items.name: Purity for smooth proper DM stacks over F_q
items.statement: For a smooth proper Deligne–Mumford stack X over F_q, H^i(X_{F̄_q}, Q_ℓ) is pure of weight i: via H^i(X) ≅ H^i(X_c) for the coarse space X_c (Rπ_*Q_ℓ = Q_ℓ, the stabilizers being finite and the coefficients of characteristic 0) and Weil II 3.3.11 for X_c, which is étale-locally a quotient of a smooth scheme by a finite group, so that Ra^!Q_ℓ = Q_ℓ(n)[2n]; or via H^i(Y)^H when X ≅ [Y/H] with Y smooth proper and H finite (for M̄_{g,n}, boggi-pikaart).
items.locator: arXiv:2206.07759v2, proof of Proposition 3.1, p. 6; proof of Proposition 4.2, p. 7
items.note: Added by FIX-RT-PAPER-BERGSTROM-FABER-PAYNE-24 (RT-PAPER-BERGSTROM-FABER-PAYNE-24/5). A global quotient presentation exists only for some DM stacks; the coarse-space route is general. The stack-to-coarse-space comparison is imported from the stacks Part II (route 7). Consumers: vdbe-theorem-2-1, vdbe-lemma-4-1, prop-3-1 and Proposition 4.2. Routed to WC.6 as a source ('extend pure cohomology … beyond projective varieties'; WC.6 requires DWP.7).

items.name: Point count of an algebraic stack
items.statement: For an algebraic stack X over F_q, X(F_q) is a finite groupoid and #X(F_q) := Σ_{x ∈ [X(F_q)]} 1/#Aut(x).
items.note: Stacks are outside the WC layers, which count points of varieties. Routed to WC.1 as a source.

items.name: Proposition 1.3(i) (additivity over stratifications)
items.statement: If X = X₀ ⊔ ⋯ ⊔ X_n is a stratification by locally closed substacks, then #X(F_q) = #X₀(F_q) + ⋯ + #X_n(F_q).
items.note: Routed to WC.1 as a source.

items.name: Proposition 1.3(ii) (quotient stacks by connected groups)
items.statement: If X = [X/G] with X a scheme and G a connected linear algebraic group, then #X(F_q) = #X(F_q)/#G(F_q).
items.note: Lang's theorem makes every G-torsor over F_q trivial. Routed to WC.1 as a source.

items.name: Proposition 1.3(iii) (DM stacks and coarse spaces)
items.statement: If X is a Deligne–Mumford stack with coarse moduli space X, then #X(F_q) = #X(F_q).
items.note: The twists of an object have masses 1/#Aut summing to 1. Routed to WC.1 as a source.

items.name: Proposition 1.3(iv) (Behrend's trace formula, DM case)
items.statement: If X is a DM stack over F_q and ℓ ∤ q, then #X(F_q) = Tr(F_q | H^•_{c,ét}(X_{F̄_q}, Q_ℓ)), the graded trace of the geometric Frobenius.
items.note: Behrend, Invent. Math. 112 (1993). For DM stacks it reduces, with Q_ℓ coefficients, to the coarse space and the trace formula for varieties. Routed to WC.1 as a source.

items.name: Polynomial point count
items.statement: A DM stack X over Z has polynomial point count if #X(F_q) is a polynomial in q (the same polynomial for all finite fields F_q).
items.note: Routed to WC as a source with the van den Bogaart–Edixhoven theorem.

items.name: van den Bogaart–Edixhoven, Theorem 2.1
items.statement: Let X be a DM stack, smooth and proper of pure relative dimension over Z. Equivalent: (i) #X(F_{p^m}) = P(p^m) + o(p^{m·dim X/2}) for some P ∈ Q[t], all p in a set of primes of Dirichlet density 1 and all m ≥ 1; (ii) #X(F_q) = P(q) for all finite fields F_q, for a polynomial P with positive integer coefficients; (iii) for all ℓ, H^•_ét(X_{Q̄}, Q_ℓ) vanishes in odd degrees and H^{2i} ≅ Q_ℓ(−i)^{⊕}. Then the coefficient of t^i is dim H^{2i}; by comparison and universal coefficients H^•(X_C, Q) is even with h^{2i} the coefficient of t^i.
items.note: Needs the Weil conjectures, the étale–singular comparison and the finite-spectrum lemma for smooth proper DM stacks over Z. Routed to WC.4/WC.5 as a source. The weights of the α_{i,j} come from deligne-purity-dm.

items.name: Specialization of étale cohomology for smooth proper DM stacks
items.statement: For X smooth and proper over Z_p and ℓ ≠ p, H^i_ét(X_{Q̄_p}, Q_ℓ) ≅ H^i_ét(X_{F̄_p}, Q_ℓ), compatibly with a lift F̃_p of the geometric Frobenius ([vdBE05, Proposition 3.1]).
items.note: Stack version of WC.4's family comparison; routed to WC.4 as a source.

items.name: van den Bogaart–Edixhoven, Lemma 4.1 (finite-spectrum lemma)
items.statement: If Σ_i (−1)^i Σ_j α_{i,j}^m = P(p^m) + o(p^{ms/2}) as m → ∞, where α_{i,j} are the Frobenius eigenvalues on H^i (of weight i), then d_i = 0 for all odd i ≥ s, and all eigenvalues on H^{2i} equal p^i for s/2 ≤ i ≤ d.
items.note: The linear-independence-of-characters argument WC.5:power-sum-converse plans in bound form. Routed there as a source. The weights of the α_{i,j} come from deligne-purity-dm.

items.name: Proposition 3.1 (approximately polynomial point counts)
items.statement: Let X be a smooth proper DM stack of relative dimension d over Z_p, F̃_p a lift of geometric Frobenius and s ≥ d an integer. If #X(F_{p^m}) = P(p^m) + o(p^{ms/2}) with P = Σ P_i t^i ∈ Q[t], then dim H^i(X_C) = 0 for all odd i ≥ s, dim H^{2i}(X_C) = P_i for s/2 ≤ i ≤ d, and all eigenvalues of F̃_p on H^{2i}_ét(X_{Q̄_p}, Q_ℓ) (ℓ ≠ p) are p^i for s/2 ≤ i ≤ d.
items.note: The proof's display should read o(p^{ms/2}) (sourceIssues E2). Routed to WC.5 as a source. The weights of the α_{i,j} come from deligne-purity-dm.

items.name: Inverse zeta function as a signed count of Frobenius-stable subsets, (8)
items.statement: For a variety Y over F_q and a partition λ, Y(λ) is the set of Frobenius-stable subsets of Y(F̄_q) with orbit type λ. Then 1/Z(Y; t) = Σ_d (Σ_{λ ⊢ d} (−1)^{ℓ(λ)} #Y(λ)) t^d (Vakil–Wood, Prop. 3.7). Definition 7.3: s_d(Y) := Σ_{λ ⊢ d} (−1)^{ℓ(λ)} #Y(λ), the coefficient of t^d; s₀(Y) = 1.
items.note: Zeta-function arithmetic, routed to WC.1 as a source.

items.name: Proposition 7.4
items.statement: If Y is nonempty and proper over F_q with H^odd_ét(Y_{F̄_q}, Q_ℓ) = 0, then s_d(Y) = 0 for d > dim H^even_ét(Y_{F̄_q}, Q_ℓ), and Σ_d s_d(Y) = 0.
items.note: 1/Z(Y; t) is a polynomial of degree dim H^even divisible by 1 − t, since F_q has eigenvalue 1 on H⁰. Routed to WC.1 as a source.

items.name: Proposition 7.1 (the naive sieve)
items.statement: Let C → V be a surjective family of curves in a variety X over F_q with all fibres reduced, and N_C := #{v ∈ V(F_q) : C_v smooth}. Then N_C = #V(F_q) + Σ_λ Σ_{Z ∈ X(λ)} (−1)^{ℓ(λ)} #{v ∈ V(F_q) : C_v singular along Z} (Bergström 2008, §6).
items.note: Routed to WC.1 as a source with the Hasse–Weil sieve.

items.name: Proposition 7.5 (the Hasse–Weil sieve)
items.statement: Let C → V be a surjective family of curves in a proper variety X over F_q, and S_d := Σ_{λ ⊢ d} Σ_{Z ∈ X(λ)} (−1)^{ℓ(λ)} #{v ∈ V(F_q) : C_v singular along Z}. If H^odd_ét((C_v^sing)_{F̄_q}, Q_ℓ) = 0 for all v ∈ V(F_q) (e.g. all fibres reduced), then S_d = 0 for d ≫ 1 and N_C = #V(F_q) + Σ_{d ≥ 1} S_d.
items.note: S_d = Σ_v s_d(C_v^sing), and Σ_d s_d(C_v^sing) is 1 or 0 by Proposition 7.4. Routed to WC.1 as a source.

items.name: Remark 7.6 (truncated sieve)
items.statement: With N_C[k] := #V(F_q) + Σ_{d ≤ k} S_d, one has N_C − N_C[k] = Σ_{d > k} S_d, estimated by stratifying V by the topological type of the fibres: F_q acts on H⁰((C_v^sing)_{F̄_q}) by roots of unity and on H² by roots of unity times q.
items.note: Routed to WC.1 as a source.

items.name: Twisted forms and their point counts
items.statement: For X over F_q and σ ∈ Aut(X) there is a unique twisted form X^σ with X^σ_{F̄_q} ≅ X_{F̄_q} identifying its geometric Frobenius with σF_q; hence the graded trace of σF_q on H^•_ét(X_{F̄_q}, Q_ℓ) is #X^σ(F_q). The construction depends on q (Remark 9.2), and conjugate σ give isomorphic forms.
items.note: Galois twisting plus the trace formula; routed to WC.1 as a source.

items.name: Definition 9.1 (equivariant point count)
items.statement: For X over F_q with an action of a finite group G, #_G X(F_q) is the element of the representation ring of G with class function σ ↦ #X^σ(F_q).
items.note: Kisin–Lehrer's equivariant counting; routed to WC.1 as a source. R(G) is representation-ring (library).

items.name: The representation ring R(G) and its character map
items.statement: For a finite group G and a field k of characteristic 0, the representation ring R(G) (the split Grothendieck ring of FDRep k G, with [V]·[W] = [V ⊗ W]) and its character ring homomorphism R(G) → (G → k), which is injective and has image the virtual characters; so an element of R(G) is determined by its class function, as Definition 9.1 requires.
items.note: Added by FIX-RT-PAPER-BERGSTROM-FABER-PAYNE-24 (RT-PAPER-BERGSTROM-FABER-PAYNE-24/7). Read at Tau Ceti f790474: repRing (RepresentationRing/Basic.lean:106) is the split K₀ of FDRep k G, which agrees with the usual R(G) for a finite group whose order is invertible in k; repRingCharacter (:127) is a ring homomorphism; range_repRingCharacter (:157) identifies its image with the virtual characters; repRingCharacter_injective (Injective.lean:50) needs [Finite G] [CharZero k].

items.name: The Frobenius characteristic in a fixed degree
items.statement: For each n, the Frobenius characteristic identifies R(S_n) with the symmetric polynomials of degree n in N ≥ n variables: the irreducible V_λ corresponds to the Schur polynomial s_λ, and p_μ = Σ_λ χ^λ(μ) s_λ.
items.locator: arXiv:2206.07759v2, §9.2, p. 23 ('writing s_λ for the Schur function that corresponds to the character of the irreducible representation V_λ')
items.note: Added by FIX-RT-PAPER-BERGSTROM-FABER-PAYNE-24 (RT-PAPER-BERGSTROM-FABER-PAYNE-24/7). SchurWeyl L7 plans this finite-variable, degree-bounded form and defers the stable ring; its ingredients are in the libraries (TauCeti.schurPoly, TauCeti.spechtChar, TauCeti.symmetricCharacterTable, TauCeti.partitionEquivSimpleModuleClasses; Mathlib MvPolynomial.psum and psumPart over a Fintype alphabet), but neither has the map ch. The stable ring BFP use is symmetric-functions-and-plethysm.

items.name: The ring of symmetric functions, the stable Frobenius characteristic and plethysm
items.statement: The graded ring Λ of symmetric functions in infinitely many variables (the inverse limit of the degree-bounded rings of symmetric polynomials) and its completion Λ̂; the stable Frobenius characteristic ch : ⊕_n R(S_n) ≅ Λ, a ring isomorphism for the induction product with ch(V_λ) = s_λ; and plethysm f ∘ g, making Λ a λ-ring with Adams operations ψ_k = p_k ∘ −, with p_n ∘ q = q^n for q a line element (e.g. the class of the Tate twist).
items.locator: arXiv:2206.07759v2, §9.2, Corollary 9.5, p. 23; proof of Proposition 9.6, p. 23; §11, pp. 25–29
items.note: Added by FIX-RT-PAPER-BERGSTROM-FABER-PAYNE-24 (RT-PAPER-BERGSTROM-FABER-PAYNE-24/7). Proposition 9.6 sums #_{S_n}M_{g,n}(F_q) over all n, so the stable ring is needed, not a fixed degree. Neither library has Λ, λ-rings or plethysm (Mathlib's Dickson.lean: 'Mathlib doesn't currently know what a Lambda ring is'). Routed to a new Part II of Tau Ceti SchurWeyl (route 8), which imports the λ-ring axiomatics from KTheoryLowDegrees Z.3 and Exp/Log from plethystic-exp-log.

items.name: Plethystic exponential and logarithm
items.statement: For a complete filtered ring with Adams operations ψ_k (for BFP, Λ̂((ħ)) with ψ_k = p_k ∘ −), Exp(f) = exp(Σ_{k≥1} ψ_k(f)/k) and Log(f) = Σ_{k≥1} (μ(k)/k) ψ_k(log f) are mutually inverse bijections between the augmentation ideal and 1 + the augmentation ideal, with Exp(f + g) = Exp(f)Exp(g).
items.locator: arXiv:2206.07759v2, §9.3, proof of Proposition 9.6, p. 23 (Getzler–Kapranov's Exp and Log)
items.note: Added by FIX-RT-PAPER-BERGSTROM-FABER-PAYNE-24 (RT-PAPER-BERGSTROM-FABER-PAYNE-24/7). The same construction as PAPER-YU-23/044 (routed to QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms QM.0, accepted) and PAPER-SCHIFFMANN-16/5 (routed to CountingBundlesAndHallAlgebrasOfCurves); HabiroNahmSeries:HB.8/integral-plethystic-logarithm is a third instance. One owner: QM.0, through YU-23's accepted route, stated for a complete filtered ring with Adams operations. Routed to QM.0 as a source (route 9).

items.name: Proposition 9.3 (equivariant polynomial counts)
items.statement: If X is smooth and proper over Z with polynomial point count and G acts over Z, then #_G X(F_q) = Σ_V P_V(q)[V] with P_V ∈ Z[t] over the irreducible representations V, and the coefficient P_{V,i} is the multiplicity of V in H^{2i}(X_C, Q).
items.note: Comparison isomorphisms are functorial, hence G-equivariant (Kisin–Lehrer, Prop. 1.2). Routed to WC.4 as a source.

items.name: Equivariant Poincaré duality for polynomial point counts (Remark 9.4)
items.statement: Let X be smooth, proper and irreducible over Z of relative dimension d, with polynomial point count P, and let a finite group G act on X over Z. Then P(t) = t^d P(1/t), and P_{V^∨}(t) = t^d P_V(t^{−1}) for every irreducible representation V of G, so P_{V,i} = P_{V,d−i} when V is self-dual.
items.locator: arXiv:2206.07759v2, Remark 9.4, first paragraph, p. 22; used in Theorem 1.4 and §10, pp. 3 and 24
items.note: Split from poincare-duality-dm by FIX-RT-PAPER-BERGSTROM-FABER-PAYNE-24 (RT-PAPER-BERGSTROM-FABER-PAYNE-24/3). The pairing is EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves EDC.2:pairings, which WC.2 imports to derive b_i = b_{2d−i}; G-equivariance follows by naturality, and P_{V,i} = [H^{2i} : V] by Proposition 9.3. Routed to WC.2 as a source.

items.name: Poincaré duality for smooth proper DM stacks, Frobenius- and G-equivariantly
items.statement: For a smooth proper Deligne–Mumford stack X of dimension d over F_q, or its coarse space, with an action of a finite group G, cup product gives a Frobenius- and G-equivariant perfect pairing H^i(X_{F̄_q}, Q_ℓ) × H^{2d−i}(X_{F̄_q}, Q_ℓ) → Q_ℓ(−d); hence the conclusions of poincare-duality-equivariant hold for M̄_{g,n} with its S_n-action.
items.note: The same theorem as PAPER-CANNING-LARSON-PAYNE-24/14. Its single owner should be EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheavesPartIIStacks (ST.1–ST.2), importing EDC.2:pairings, as FIX-RT-AREA-etale /3 recommends and the verifier of RT-PAPER-BERGSTROM-FABER-PAYNE-24/3 requires; SF.2 does not own duality. Routed there by route 7. With Q_ℓ coefficients the moduli case also reduces to schemes: H^•(M̄_{g,n}) = H^•(X_{g,n})^H by boggi-pikaart, and EDC.2's pairing on X_{g,n} restricts to a perfect pairing on H-invariants.

items.name: Weight spectral sequence of a normal crossings compactification
items.statement: For M_{g,n} ⊂ M̄_{g,n} with normal crossings boundary stratified by stable graphs G, there is a spectral sequence with E₁^{j,k} = ⊕_{|E(G)| = j} (H^k(∏_v M̄_{g_v,n_v}) ⊗ det E(G))^{Aut(G)} = H^k(D̃^{(j)}, ε^j), where D̃^{(j)} = ⊔_{|E(G)|=j} M̃_G and ε^j is the determinant of the local system of the j boundary branches, identified with the sign of the permutation action of Aut(G) on E(G); it abuts to H^{j+k}_c(M_{g,n}) and degenerates at E₂ (Payne–Willwacher §2.3; Deligne, Hodge II §3.2, dual form). In ℓ-adic cohomology after base change to F̄_p it is a spectral sequence of Galois representations (Petersen 2017, Ex. 3.5), and Frobenius acts trivially on det E(G), because the branches are defined over Z.
items.locator: arXiv:2206.07759v2, proof of Proposition 4.2, (3), p. 7; proof of Corollary 9.5, p. 23
items.note: DWP.8 plans weight filtrations of mixed complexes; Deligne's weight spectral sequence for the complement of a normal crossings divisor in a smooth proper DM stack is its geometric instance. Routed to DWP.8 as a source. The paper's (3) omits det E(G) (sourceIssues E7; RT-PAPER-BERGSTROM-FABER-PAYNE-24/2): the untwisted page gives χ_c(M_{1,2}) = 2, but #M_{1,2}(F_q) = q², so χ_c = 1. With one edge the sign is trivial, so the (0, k) and (1, k) columns used by ac-lemma-2-6 are unaffected.

items.name: Counting squarefree polynomials over F_q
items.statement: Let P_g be the set of squarefree polynomials over F_q of degree 2g + 2 or 2g + 1. Unique factorization f = h·m² (h squarefree, m monic) gives (q − 1)(q^{2g+2} + q^{2g+1}) = Σ_{j=0}^{g} #P_{g−j} q^j + (q − 1)q^{g+1}; with #P₀ = q²(q − 1), induction gives #P_g = (q − 1)(q^{2g+2} − q^{2g}) for g ≥ 1.
items.note: The monic count s_n (s_0 = 1, s_1 = q, s_n = q^n − q^{n−1}) is FF.3's, next to FF.3/gauss-count-formula; ArithmeticStatistics:ST.4/count-of-squarefree-monic-polynomials-over-a-finite-field duplicates it and should import it; #P_g = (q − 1)(s_{2g+2} + s_{2g+1}) (RT-PAPER-BERGSTROM-FABER-PAYNE-24/4, as its verifier corrected it). Routed to FF.3 as a source.

items.name: Vanishing of quadratic-character correlation sums by interpolation
items.statement: For d ≥ 2 and distinct x ≠ y ∈ P¹(F_q), q odd: Σ_{deg f ≤ d} χ(f(x)) χ(f(y)) = 0, summing over all polynomials of degree ≤ d (evaluation at ∞ via the degree-d coefficient).
items.note: Evaluation at two points is surjective from polynomials of degree ≤ d ≥ 1, so the sum factors as Σχ · Σχ = 0. Routed to FF.1 as a source.

items.name: Reduced irreducible quadric surfaces over F_q
items.statement: There are exactly three PGL₄(F_q)-orbits of reduced irreducible quadric surfaces in P³ over F_q: a cone Q^con ≅ P(1,1,2); a non-split smooth quadric Q^nsp of Picard rank 1, which becomes P¹ × P¹ over F_{q²} with Frobenius swapping the rulings; and the split quadric Q^spl ≅ P¹ × P¹. Automorphism groups (6): #Aut(Q^con) = q⁷ − q⁶ − q⁵ + q⁴, #Aut(Q^nsp) = 2(q⁶ − q²), #Aut(Q^spl) = 2(q³ − q)². Each automorphism extends to PGL₄ as the hyperplane series is complete.
items.note: The finite-field case of the classification of quadratic forms (rank, and discriminant or Arf invariant), with the orders of the projective orthogonal groups; routed to GN.2 as a source. The orders were rechecked: |Aut P(1,1,2)| = |GL₂(F_q)|·q³ and |PGL₂(F_{q²})|·2.

items.name: Moduli stacks of stable pointed curves (Knudsen)
items.statement: For g, n ≥ 0 with 2g − 2 + n > 0, M_{g,n} ⊂ M̄_{g,n} are the moduli stacks of smooth and of stable n-pointed genus g curves: smooth and proper Deligne–Mumford stacks over Z, whose boundary ∂M̄_{g,n} := M̄_{g,n} ∖ M_{g,n} is a divisor with normal crossings relative to Z, with universal curve M̄_{g,n+1} → M̄_{g,n} given by forgetting the last point.
items.locator: arXiv:2206.07759v2, §1, p. 2; §2, p. 4; proof of Proposition 3.1, p. 6; proof of Proposition 4.2, p. 7
items.note: Imported from StableReductionPartII, the single owner of pointed stable-curve moduli (FIX-RT-AREA-etale /4); routed there by route 6 (RT-PAPER-BERGSTROM-FABER-PAYNE-24/1). The paper needs every (g, n) with 2g − 2 + n > 0, including Keel's M̄_{0,n} and M̄_{1,11} for the sharpness of Theorem 1.1; PAPER-YUAN-26 route 10's brief still reads 'for g>1' until FIX-RT-AREA-etale's Edit 1 (the pointed range) is applied. Stable pointed curves and dual graphs come from Tau Ceti StableReduction Layers 1 and 3. The boundary stratification is the separate item boundary-strata.

items.name: Boundary strata of M̄_{g,n} by stable graphs
items.statement: ∂M̄_{g,n} is stratified by marked dual graphs G (stable graphs of genus g with n legs): the open strata are M_G ≅ (∏_{v ∈ V(G)} M_{g_v,n_v})/Aut(G), and the normalized closed strata are M̃_G ≅ (∏_{v ∈ V(G)} M̄_{g_v,n_v})/Aut(G), so that with constant coefficients H^•(M̃_G) = (⊗_v H^•(M̄_{g_v,n_v}))^{Aut(G)}.
items.locator: arXiv:2206.07759v2, §4, Notation 4.1 and proof of Proposition 4.2, pp. 6–7
items.note: Split from moduli-stacks by FIX-RT-PAPER-BERGSTROM-FABER-PAYNE-24 (RT-PAPER-BERGSTROM-FABER-PAYNE-24/1). Plain Aut(G)-invariants are right here, for the open-strata decomposition used by Proposition 4.2(3) and for the Getzler–Kapranov formula of Proposition 9.6; only the E₁ page of the weight spectral sequence carries the sign det E(G) (weight-spectral-sequence; sourceIssues E7).

items.name: M̄_{g,n} as a global finite quotient
items.statement: M̄_{g,n} can be realized S_n-equivariantly as the global quotient [X_{g,n}/H] of a smooth and proper variety X_{g,n} by a finite group H (Boggi–Pikaart 2000). BFP use it over F_q, for every q, to form the twisted forms [X^σ_{g,n}/H] of Remark 9.4, and over Q for the pure-Tate remark of §1.
items.note: The extraction's earlier wording 'smooth projective … over Q' is not the paper's: Remark 9.4 (p. 22) says 'smooth and proper'. The base over which BP00 (Compositio 120 (2000), 171–191) constructs X_{g,n}, and whether it is projective there, must be taken from BP00 itself; the fixer could not obtain it (Springer subscription). Routed with moduli-stacks to StableReductionPartII (route 6): it is a finite level-structure cover of M̄_{g,n}, of the same kind as the projective finite scheme covers of PAPER-YUAN-26 route 10 and de Jong's covers, and says nothing about cohomology (RT-PAPER-BERGSTROM-FABER-PAYNE-24/1).

items.name: Polynomial point count forces pure Tate Hodge structures
items.statement: If a smooth proper DM stack X over Z has polynomial point count and its coarse space over Q is a finite quotient of a smooth projective variety (as for M̄_{g,n}), then H^•(X_C, Q) is even and the Hodge structure on it is pure Tate.
items.note: Inputs: the Boggi–Pikaart presentation (the coarse space is Y/H with Y smooth and proper, so H^•(X_C, Q) = H^•(Y)^H carries a pure Hodge structure); the Hodge decomposition of smooth projective complex varieties, which the atlas plans only in the draft SeveralComplexVariablesKahlerGeometry CV.5, with Tau Ceti HodgeStructures L0 (an import gap, recorded in route 1's brief); and the Hodge–Tate/de Rham comparison CohomologyComparisons CP.3 (or Katz's E-polynomial theorem) to pass from 'H^{2i}_ét is a sum of Q_ℓ(−i)' to Hodge type (i, i). No mixed Hodge structure is needed (RT-PAPER-BERGSTROM-FABER-PAYNE-24/6). Routed to the moduli-of-curves roadmap with its only application.

items.name: The excision sequence of the boundary
items.statement: · · · → H^k_c(M_{g,n}) → H^k(M̄_{g,n}) → H^k(∂M̄_{g,n}) → H^{k+1}_c(M_{g,n}) → · · ·, rational (compactly supported) cohomology.
items.note: CLP24's brief plans the boundary sequences; routed to that roadmap.

items.name: Arbarello–Cornalba, Lemma 2.6
items.statement: If H^k_c(M_{g,n}) = 0, then pullback to the normalization of the boundary gives an injection H^k(M̄_{g,n}) ↪ H^k(∂̃M̄_{g,n}).
items.note: For M̄_{g,n} this is the (0, k) corner of the weight spectral sequence: by E₂-degeneration, ker(H^k(M̄_{g,n}) → H^k(∂̃M̄_{g,n})) = E_2^{0,k} = gr^W_k H^k_c(M_{g,n}); one-edge graphs carry no sign twist. Inputs: weight-spectral-sequence (DWP.8), deligne-purity-dm, etale-singular-comparison (WC.4). AC98 argue with Hodge III 8.2.5, but the atlas plans no mixed Hodge structure on the cohomology of varieties, so the formalization follows the ℓ-adic route (RT-PAPER-BERGSTROM-FABER-PAYNE-24/6, as its verifier corrected it). Routed to the moduli-of-curves roadmap.

items.name: Harer: virtual cohomological dimension of M_{g,n}
items.statement: For g ≥ 2, vcd(M_g) = 4g − 5; for g ≥ 1, vcd(M_{g,1}) = 4g − 3 and vcd(M_{g,n}) = 4g − 4 + n for n ≥ 1; hence H^k(M_{g,n}; Q) = 0 above the vcd.
items.note: CLP24's brief asks for the vcd as its own layer; routed there.

items.name: Vanishing in the virtual cohomological dimension
items.statement: H^{4g−5}(M_g; Q) = 0 (Church–Farb–Putman 2012; Morita–Sakasai–Suzuki 2013) and H^{4g−3}(M_{g,1}; Q) = 0.
items.locator: arXiv:2206.07759v2, proof of Proposition 2.1, p. 5; Remark 2.4, p. 5
items.note: Routed to the moduli-of-curves roadmap beside the vcd.

items.name: Proposition 2.1 (vanishing of compactly supported cohomology)
items.statement: For g ≥ 1: H^k_c(M_{g,n}) = 0 for k < 2g when n = 0, 1, and for k < 2g − 2 + n when n ≥ 2.
items.note: Poincaré duality with the vcd (AC98, (2.4)) for n ≥ 2; for n = 0, 1 the extra degree comes from cfp-mss. Routed to the moduli-of-curves roadmap.

items.name: Arbarello–Cornalba, Lemma 2.9 (the inductive method)
items.statement: Let k be odd. If H^q(M̄_{g,n}) = 0 for all odd q ≤ k and all (g, n) with H^q_c(M_{g,n}) ≠ 0, then H^q(M̄_{g,n}) = 0 for all odd q ≤ k and all g, n.
items.note: Routed to the moduli-of-curves roadmap.

items.name: Arbarello–Cornalba: vanishing in degrees 1, 3, 5
items.statement: H^q(M̄_{g,n}; Q) = 0 for q ∈ {1, 3, 5}, for all g and n ([AC98, Theorem 2.1]).
items.note: Routed to the moduli-of-curves roadmap.

items.name: Keel: cohomology of M̄_{0,n}
items.statement: H^•(M̄_{0,n}; Q) is supported in even degrees (Keel 1992).
items.note: Routed to the moduli-of-curves roadmap.

items.name: Polynomial point counts in genus ≤ 3
items.statement: M̄_{g,n} has polynomial point count for g = 1, n ≤ 10 (Getzler 1998); g = 2, n ≤ 7 (Bergström 2009, §11.2); g = 3, n ≤ 5 (Bergström 2008); and M_{1,n} for 4 ≤ n ≤ 7.
items.locator: arXiv:2206.07759v2, proof of Theorem 1.1, p. 5; proof of Proposition 8.8 (D), p. 19
items.note: Cited inputs; routed to the moduli-of-curves roadmap.

items.name: Theorem 1.1 for k = 7
items.statement: H^k(M̄_{g,n}; Q) = 0 for all odd k ≤ 7 and all g, n. The base cases g ≥ 1, max{2g, 2g − 2 + n} ≤ 7 all have polynomial point count, as do all g ≤ 3 with 2g − 2 + n ≤ 9.
items.locator: arXiv:2206.07759v2, §2, proof of Theorem 1.1 for k = 7, p. 5
items.note: Routed to the moduli-of-curves roadmap.

items.name: Theorem 1.1 (odd cohomology vanishing)
items.statement: H^k(M̄_{g,n}; Q) = 0 for all odd k ≤ 9 and all g, n. The bound is sharp: H^{11}(M̄_{1,11}) ≅ Q².
items.locator: arXiv:2206.07759v2, §1, Theorem 1.1, p. 1; §2, proof for k = 9 from Theorem 1.4, p. 5
items.note: k = 9 needs only H⁹(M̄_{4,n}) = 0 for n ≤ 3 (Theorem 1.4, or Corollary 3.2). This is the input the CLP24 brief names as 'the vanishing of the low-degree Borel–Moore homology of M_{g,n} proved by Bergström–Faber–Payne'. Routed to that roadmap.

items.name: Corollary 3.2
items.statement: If #M̄_{4,n}(F_q) = P(q) + o(q^{9/2+n}) for q = p^m, m → ∞, with P ∈ Q[t], then H^k(M̄_{4,n}) = 0 for all odd k ≤ 9.
items.note: Proposition 3.1 with s = 9 + 2n and Poincaré duality. The printed conclusion says M̄_{g,n} (sourceIssues E1). Routed to the moduli-of-curves roadmap.

items.name: Notation 4.1 (the order ≺)
items.statement: (g′, n′) ≺ (g, n) if (g′, n′) <_lex (g, n) and 2g′ + n′ ≤ 2g + n. Each boundary stratum of M̄_{g,n} is a finite quotient (∏_i M_{g_i,n_i})/G with (g_i, n_i) ≺ (g, n).
items.note: Routed to the moduli-of-curves roadmap.

items.name: Proposition 4.2(1)
items.statement: If M̄_{g′,n′} has polynomial point count for all (g′, n′) ≺ (g, n), every eigenvalue of F_p on H^•_{c,ét}((M_{g′,n′})_{F̄_p}, Q_ℓ), (g′, n′) ≺ (g, n), is a power of p.
items.note: Via the weight spectral sequence. Routed to the moduli-of-curves roadmap.

items.name: Proposition 4.2(2)
items.statement: Under the same hypothesis, M_{g′,n′} has polynomial point count for all (g′, n′) ≺ (g, n).
items.note: Routed to the moduli-of-curves roadmap.

items.name: Proposition 4.2(3)
items.statement: Under the same hypothesis, the boundary divisor ∂M̄_{g,n} has polynomial point count.
items.note: Routed to the moduli-of-curves roadmap.

items.name: The hyperelliptic stack as a quotient
items.statement: Over Z[1/2], the stack H_g of hyperelliptic curves of genus g is the quotient of the space of binary forms of degree 2g + 2 with nonvanishing discriminant by a connected linear algebraic group G with #G(F_q) = (q² − 1)(q² − q) (Arsie–Vistoli 2004, Cor. 4.7); dehomogenizing identifies these forms with P_g.
items.note: Routed to the moduli-of-curves roadmap.

items.name: Point count of H_g, (4)
items.statement: For g ≥ 2 and q odd, #H_g(F_q) = #P_g/#G(F_q) = q^{2g−1} (cf. Brock–Granville 2001, Prop. 7.1); the same holds for all q.
items.note: Routed to the moduli-of-curves roadmap.

items.name: Lemma 5.2
items.statement: For q odd, Σ_{C ∈ [H_g(F_q)]} (q + 1 − #C(F_q))^k / #Aut(C) equals 0 for k odd and q^{2g} − 1 for k = 2.
items.note: Odd k: the quadratic twist C_f ↦ C_{tf} flips the sign. k = 2: expand (Σ_x χ(f(x)))²; the diagonal gives q^{2g}#G(F_q) and the off-diagonal gives −#G(F_q). Routed to the moduli-of-curves roadmap.

items.name: Proposition 5.1 (pointed hyperelliptic counts)
items.note: Proved for odd q from Lemma 5.2; all q by Bergström 2009, Thm. 10.3. Rechecked by expanding #C(#C − 1)(#C − 2) in q + 1 − #C. Routed to the moduli-of-curves roadmap.

items.name: Canonical genus 4 curves as (2, 3) complete intersections
items.statement: The canonical image of a non-hyperelliptic genus 4 curve is a complete intersection of a quadric and a cubic in P³; the quadric is unique, reduced and irreducible. Conversely every smooth (2, 3) complete intersection is a canonical genus 4 curve. Hence M₄ ∖ H₄ ≅ [S₂₃/PGL₄] and (5): #(M₄ ∖ H₄)(F_q) = #S₂₃(F_q)/#PGL₄(F_q).
items.note: Routed to the moduli-of-curves roadmap.

items.name: Propositions 6.1–6.2 (counting by the quadric)
items.statement: With N^•_n(q) the number of smooth (2, 3) complete intersections C on a fixed Q^• (• ∈ {con, nsp, spl}; on Q^con, curves of degree 6 not through the vertex) with n distinct marked points in C(F_q), #(M_{4,n} ∖ H_{4,n})(F_q) = Σ_• N^•_n(q)/#Aut(Q^•) for n ≤ 3 (n = 0 is Proposition 6.1).
items.note: Orbit–stabilizer over the three quadric orbits. Routed to the moduli-of-curves roadmap.

items.name: Examples 7.7–7.9 (non-reduced fibres on the three quadrics)
items.statement: For the families of (2, 3) complete intersections on Q^con (V ≅ A^{15}, cubics avoiding the vertex), Q^nsp and Q^spl (V ≅ P^{15}), the singular locus of every non-reduced fibre has no odd cohomology, so Proposition 7.5 applies. s(P¹) = (1, −1 − q, q), and N_C[k] = N_C^red[k] for k ≥ 2, 4, 5 respectively.
items.note: Routed to the moduli-of-curves roadmap.

items.name: Inverse zeta functions of the quadrics
items.statement: 1/Z(X; t) = (1 − qt)(1 − q²t) for X = (Q^con)^sm = A² ⊔ A¹; 1/Z(Q^nsp; t) = (1 − t)(1 − qt)(1 + qt)(1 − q²t), so s₁..s₄ = −q² − 1, 0, q⁴ + q², −q⁴; 1/Z(Q^spl; t) = (1 − t)(1 − qt)²(1 − q²t), so s₁..s₃ = −q² − 2q − 1, 2(q³ + q² + q), −q⁴ − 2q³ − q².
items.note: Routed to the moduli-of-curves roadmap.

items.name: Proposition 8.1 (sieve on the cone, n = 0)
items.note: Routed to the moduli-of-curves roadmap.

items.name: Proposition 8.2 (sieve on the cone, n ≤ 3)
items.statement: The terms S_d(C^con_n) for d, n ≤ 3 are the twelve polynomials tabulated on p. 14 (e.g. S₀(C^con₁) = q^{16} + q^{15}, S₁(C^con₁) = −q^{15} − 3q^{14} − q^{13} + q^{12}, S₂(C^con₁) = 2q^{13} + q^{12} − q^{11}, S₃(C^con₁) = 0).
items.note: S₀–S₂ for n = 1 were rechecked from the proof's formulas. Routed to the moduli-of-curves roadmap.

items.name: Propositions 8.4–8.5 (sieve on the non-split quadric)
items.statement: S₀(C^nsp) = p₁₅, S₁ = (−q² − 1)p₁₂, S₂ = 0, S₃ = (q⁴ + q²)p₆ with p_n = #P^n(F_q), since up to three singularities impose independent conditions; and the terms S_d(C^nsp_n), d, n ≤ 3, tabulated on p. 16.
items.note: Routed to the moduli-of-curves roadmap.

items.name: Propositions 8.6–8.7 (sieve on the split quadric)
items.statement: S₀(C^spl) = p₁₅, S₁ = (−q² − 2q − 1)p₁₂, S₂ = 2(q³ + q² + q)p₉, S₃ = (−q⁴ − 2q³ − q²)p₆; and S_d(C^spl_n) for d, n ≤ 3 up to o(q⁶), tabulated on p. 17.
items.note: Routed to the moduli-of-curves roadmap.

items.name: Proposition 8.8 (four or more singularities)
items.statement: For • ∈ {con, nsp, spl}: Σ_{d ≥ 4} S_d(C^•_n)/#Aut(Q^•) = o(q^{(9+n)/2}) for n ≤ 2, and = Bq⁶ + o(q⁶) for n = 3 with B an integer.
items.note: Proof: non-reduced curves (Examples 7.7–7.9); reducible families (A)–(F) whose contributions cancel through s_k(P¹) = 0 and s_k(A¹) = 0 for k ≥ 2; the count of 4-tuples in general position (item gp-4-tuples). Routed to the moduli-of-curves roadmap.

items.name: Signed count of 4-tuples in general position on P¹ × P¹
items.statement: The Hasse–Weil (signed) count of 4-tuples of points of Q^spl in general position (no two on a ruling, not all on an irreducible (1,1)-curve) is (q + 1)²q²(q − 1)² = #(PGL₂ × PGL₂)(F_q).
items.locator: arXiv:2206.07759v2, proof of Proposition 8.8, p. 20; Remark 8.11, p. 21
items.note: PGL₂ × PGL₂ acts freely, the count is q⁶ + O(q⁵), and Remark 8.11 gives a direct orbit-type check. Routed to the moduli-of-curves roadmap.

items.name: Weight-graded equivariant Euler characteristic
items.statement: For M_{g,n}, the S_n-equivariant weight-graded Euler characteristic Σ_i (−1)^i gr^W_{2k} H^i_c(M_{g,n}, Q) as a virtual representation, and gr^W_• of the weight filtration.
items.note: Routed to the moduli-of-curves roadmap.

items.name: Twisted forms of M̄_{g,n} and M_{g,λ}
items.statement: For fixed q and σ ∈ S_n, M̄^σ_{g,n} := [X^σ_{g,n}/H], a smooth proper DM stack over F_q representing families of stable curves with n labelled geometric sections permuted by Frobenius via σ. For λ ⊢ n, σ(λ) fixes the first n₁ points, transposes the next n₂ pairs, and so on; M_{g,λ}, H_{g,λ}, ∂M̄_{g,λ} are defined likewise, with M̄_{g,λ} = M_{g,λ} ⊔ ∂M̄_{g,λ}.
items.note: Routed to the moduli-of-curves roadmap.

items.name: Corollary 9.5 (equivariant counts of the open part)
items.statement: If M̄_{g′,n′} has polynomial point count for (g′, n′) ⪯ (g, n), then #_{S_n} M_{g,n}(F_q) = Σ_{λ ⊢ n} P_λ(q)s_λ with P_λ ∈ Z[t], and the coefficient of t^k in P_λ is the multiplicity of V_λ in Σ_i (−1)^i gr^W_{2k} H^i_c(M_{g,n}, Q).
items.note: Routed to the moduli-of-curves roadmap. The s_λ are those of frobenius-characteristic and symmetric-functions-and-plethysm.

items.name: Getzler–Kapranov formula and its point-count version
items.statement: For a stable S-module V, Ch(MV) = Log(exp(Δ) Exp(Ch V)) (Getzler–Kapranov 1998, Thm. 8.13). Applied to point counts via p_n ∘ q = q^n, with Ch(V) = Σ_{2(g−1)+n>0} h^{g−1} #_{S_n}M_{g,n}(F_q), Ch(MV) − Ch(V) = Σ h^{g−1} #_{S_n}∂M̄_{g,n}(F_q): the equivariant boundary counts are determined by #_{S_{n′}}M_{g′,n′}(F_q), (g′, n′) ≺ (g, n).
items.locator: arXiv:2206.07759v2, §9.3, proof of Proposition 9.6, p. 23; §11, p. 25
items.note: The §9 introduction cites it as Theorem 8.3 (sourceIssues E5). Routed to the moduli-of-curves roadmap. Λ̂, plethysm and p_n ∘ q = q^n come from symmetric-functions-and-plethysm, Exp and Log from plethystic-exp-log; stable S-modules, Ch, the Laplacian Δ and Theorem 8.13 stay here.

items.name: Equivariant counts in genus ≤ 3
items.statement: The S_{n′}-equivariant point counts of M_{g′,n′} are known for g′ = 0 (Kisin–Lehrer 2002) and for 1 ≤ g′ ≤ 3 with (g′, n′) ≺ (4, 3) (Getzler 1998; Bergström 2008, 2009).
items.note: Cited inputs; routed to the moduli-of-curves roadmap.

items.name: Proposition 9.6 (boundary counts in genus 4)
items.note: Computed with Maple/SF from the Getzler–Kapranov formula, inductively in n. Rechecked here against Theorems 1.4 and 1.5: M̄ − M − ∂ = 0 for n ≤ 3. Routed to the moduli-of-curves roadmap.

items.name: Gorsky's equivariant Euler characteristic
items.statement: The S_n-equivariant Euler characteristic of M_{g,n} (Gorsky 2014); in particular χ(M_{4,3}) = −10 and χ_{S₃}(M_{4,3}) = 2s₃ − 6s_{2,1}.
items.note: Cited input; both values rechecked against Theorems 1.5 and 11.1. Routed to the moduli-of-curves roadmap.

items.name: Theorem 1.4 (point counts of M̄_{4,n})
items.statement: For n ≤ 3, #M̄_{4,n}(F_q) is a polynomial in q: #M̄₄(F_q) = q⁹ + 4q⁸ + 13q⁷ + 32q⁶ + 50q⁵ + 50q⁴ + 32q³ + 13q² + 4q + 1; #M̄_{4,1}(F_q) = q^{10} + 6q⁹ + 30q⁸ + 93q⁷ + 191q⁶ + 240q⁵ + 191q⁴ + 93q³ + 30q² + 6q + 1; #M̄_{4,2}(F_q) = q^{11} + 11q^{10} + 76q⁹ + 319q⁸ + 838q⁷ + 1362q⁶ + ⋯ + 11q + 1; #M̄_{4,3}(F_q) = q^{12} + 21q^{11} + 207q^{10} + 1168q⁹ + 3977q⁸ + 8296q⁷ + 10605q⁶ + ⋯ + 21q + 1 (elided terms by Poincaré duality). Consequently H^•(M̄_{4,n}) is pure Tate with these Poincaré polynomials (in t²).
items.note: Routed to the moduli-of-curves roadmap.

items.name: Theorem 1.5 (point counts of M_{4,n})
items.note: Routed to the moduli-of-curves roadmap.

items.name: Euler characteristics in Grothendieck groups
items.statement: Replacing q by Q_ℓ(−1) (resp. Q(−1)) in Theorem 1.5 gives e_c(M_{4,n} ⊗ Q̄, Q_ℓ) in the Grothendieck group of ℓ-adic Galois representations (Bergström 2008, Thm. 3.2) and e_c((M_{4,n})_C, Q) in that of mixed Hodge structures (Tommasi 2005; Bergström–Tommasi 2007); e.g. e_c(M₄) = Q_ℓ(−9) + Q_ℓ(−8) + Q_ℓ(−7) − Q_ℓ(−6).
items.note: Routed to the moduli-of-curves roadmap.

items.name: §10: assembling Theorems 1.4 and 1.5
items.statement: N^con = q^{15} − q^{14} − q^{13} + q^{12} + o(q^{23/2}), N^nsp = q^{15} − q^{12} − q^{11} + o(q^{21/2}) and N^spl = q^{15} − 2q^{13} − q^{12} + q^{11} + o(q^{21/2}), so #(M₄ ∖ H₄)(F_q) = q⁹ + q⁸ − q⁶ + o(q^{9/2}). Adding #H₄ and #∂M̄₄ determines #M̄₄ up to o(q^{9/2}), hence exactly by van den Bogaart–Edixhoven and Poincaré duality; similarly for n = 1, 2. For n = 3 the q⁶ coefficient B = 10605 is fixed by χ(M_{4,3}) = −10.
items.note: Rechecked by computer from Propositions 5.1, 8.1–8.7 and 9.6 for n = 0, 1, 2: the resulting M̄_{4,n} agree with Theorem 1.4 in all degrees ≥ (9+n)/2. The printed M_{4,3} display has −11q⁴ for −11q³ (sourceIssues E3). Routed to the moduli-of-curves roadmap.

items.name: Equivariant hyperelliptic counts (§11.1)
items.statement: #_{S₂}H_{4,2}(F_q) = (q⁹ + q⁸ − 1)s₂ + q⁸s_{1²} and #_{S₃}H_{4,3}(F_q) = (q^{10} + q⁹ − q⁸ − q)s₃ + (q⁹ − q)s_{2,1} (Bergström 2009).
items.note: Consistent with Proposition 5.1 for g = 4. Routed to the moduli-of-curves roadmap.

items.name: Propositions 11.2–11.4 (twisted sieve terms)
items.statement: The sieve terms S_d(C^•_λ) for • ∈ {con, nsp, spl}, λ ∈ {[2], [2,1], [3]}, d ≤ 3 are the polynomials tabulated on pp. 26–28 (the nsp and spl ones up to o(q⁶)).
items.note: The S₀ terms come from counts of Frobenius-conjugate pairs and triples: q⁴ − q, q⁴ + q², q⁴ + q² − 2q pairs and q⁶ + q³ − q² − q, q⁶ − q², q⁶ + 2q³ − q² − 2q triples on Q^con, Q^nsp, Q^spl (rechecked). Routed to the moduli-of-curves roadmap.

routes.title: Tautological rings and motivic structures in the cohomology of moduli of stable curves
routes.brief: This is the new roadmap proposed by PAPER-CANNING-LARSON-PAYNE-24 under the same id, accepted on review; its brief remains binding. That brief already asks for 'the vanishing of the low-degree Borel–Moore homology of M_{g,n} proved by Bergström–Faber–Payne' as a layer, and this paper supplies it with its point-counting proof. Import the moduli stacks M_{g,n} ⊂ M̄_{g,n}, their properness, smoothness and normal-crossings boundary, and the Boggi–Pikaart presentation from StableReductionPartII; after the boundary-stratification and vcd layers add: the Arbarello–Cornalba method (excision sequence, Lemma 2.6 (derived from DWP.8's weight spectral sequence, not from Hodge III), Lemma 2.9, vanishing in degrees 1, 3, 5), Keel's theorem, Church–Farb–Putman and Morita–Sakasai–Suzuki, Proposition 2.1; polynomial point counts of M̄_{g,n} and Proposition 4.2 (via DWP.8's weight spectral sequence). Only the E₁ page of the weight spectral sequence, a sum over the normalized closed strata M̃_G, carries the sign det E(G) of the boundary branches (E7); the decomposition of ∂M̄_{g,n} into open strata M_G = (∏_v M_{g_v,n_v})/Aut(G), Proposition 4.2(3) and the Getzler–Kapranov formula of Proposition 9.6 take plain Aut(G)-invariants; the hyperelliptic stack (Arsie–Vistoli) and the counts of §5; canonical genus 4 curves on the three quadrics (§6, with GN.2's classification); the genus 4 sieve computations of §8, Proposition 8.8 included; equivariant counts of M̄_{g,n} through twisted forms, stable S-modules with their characteristic Ch and the Laplacian Δ, the Getzler–Kapranov formula (Theorem 8.13) and Gorsky's Euler characteristic (§9); the assembly of §10; Theorems 1.1, 1.4, 1.5, 11.1 and 11.5, with the symplectic local systems V_λ on M₄. Import from WeilConjectures the stack point counts (Behrend), the van den Bogaart–Edixhoven theorem, Proposition 3.1, the Hasse–Weil sieve and equivariant counts (WC.1, WC.2, WC.4, WC.5), and from FiniteFieldsAndCharacterSums the squarefree and character-sum lemmas. Import R(G) (Tau Ceti repRing, in the library) and the fixed-degree Frobenius characteristic (Tau Ceti SchurWeyl L7); the ring Λ of symmetric functions, the stable characteristic and plethysm from the SchurWeyl Part II of route 8; plethystic Exp and Log from QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms QM.0; purity for DM stacks from WC.6 and Poincaré duality for DM stacks from the stacks Part II of route 7. Import gap: the pure-Tate remark needs the Hodge decomposition of smooth projective complex varieties, planned only in the draft SeveralComplexVariablesKahlerGeometry CV.5 (with Tau Ceti HodgeStructures L0), and the Hodge–Tate comparison CohomologyComparisons CP.3. Acceptance: Theorems 1.4 and 1.5 differ by Proposition 9.6 in every degree; the closed counts are palindromic; χ(M_{4,3}) = −10 and χ_{S₃}(M_{4,3}) = 2s₃ − 6s_{2,1}; and H^{11}(M̄_{1,11}) ≅ Q² shows Theorem 1.1 is sharp.
routes.reason: The moduli stacks themselves belong to StableReductionPartII (route 6); PAPER-CANNING-LARSON-PAYNE-24 proposed this roadmap for the cohomology of M̄_{g,n}, and its design (DESIGN-MotivicStructuresInModuliOfCurves) is pending. Its brief names this paper's vanishing theorem as a planned layer, and Canning–Larson–Payne's own proofs start from it, so the whole moduli-theoretic content coalesces there, keeping its id, title and area.

DWP.8 plans weight filtrations of mixed ℓ-adic complexes. The weight spectral sequence of a normal crossings compactification of a smooth DM stack, with E₁ built from normalized boundary strata, is its geometric instance. The paper uses its Galois-equivariant form (Petersen; Payne–Willwacher), so it is a source for DWP.8. Its E₁ term carries the orientation local system of the boundary branches, E₁^{j,k} = ⊕_{|E(G)|=j} (H^k(M̄_G) ⊗ det E(G))^{Aut(G)}, which the paper's display (3) omits (E7).

Two elementary finite-field lemmas behind the hyperelliptic counts belong with characters and polynomial counting: the vanishing of quadratic-character correlation sums by interpolation (FF.1), and the count of squarefree polynomials of degree 2g + 1 or 2g + 2 through f = h·m² (FF.3, which plans the counting theory of polynomials over F_q: Gauss's count formula and the prime polynomial theorem; the ArithmeticStatistics ST.4 node for the same count should import it).

GN.2 integrates the classification of quadratic forms by discriminants and local invariants. The three PGL₄(F_q)-orbits of reduced irreducible quadric surfaces and the orders of their automorphism groups are its finite-field case, including characteristic 2 through the Arf invariant.

routes.title: Representations of the symmetric group, Specht modules, and Schur-Weyl duality, Part II: the ring of symmetric functions, the stable Frobenius characteristic and plethysm
routes.brief: Start where Tau Ceti SchurWeyl Layer 7 stops: it plans the Frobenius characteristic in a fixed degree and finitely many variables and defers 'the stable symmetric-function ring and the Hall inner product'. Construct the graded ring Λ of symmetric functions in infinitely many variables as the inverse limit of the degree-bounded rings of Layer 7, its completion Λ̂, the monomial, elementary, complete, power-sum and Schur bases, and the Hall inner product. Prove that the stable Frobenius characteristic ⊕_n R(S_n) → Λ is a ring isomorphism for the induction product with ch(V_λ) = s_λ, compatible with Layer 7 in each degree and with Tau Ceti repRing. Construct plethysm f ∘ g and the λ-ring structure on Λ with Adams operations ψ_k = p_k ∘ −, importing the λ-ring axiomatics from KTheoryLowDegrees Z.3 rather than redefining them, and prove p_n ∘ q = q^n for a line element q. Import plethystic Exp and Log from QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms QM.0. Acceptance: ch(V_{(n)}) = h_n and ch(sgn) = e_n; p_2 ∘ s_{1,1} = s_{2,2} − s_{2,1,1} + s_{1,1,1,1}; Exp and Log are inverse on Λ̂'s augmentation ideal. Consumers: MotivicStructuresInModuliOfCurves (Getzler–Kapranov) and HabiroRings (its free Λ-ring gap). This Part II is distinct from SchurWeylIntegralFunctors (PAPER-CADORET-HUI-TAMAGAWA-17 route 3), which concerns integral Young symmetrizers.
routes.reason: Neither pinned library has the ring of symmetric functions, λ-rings or plethysm, and SchurWeyl Layer 7 defers the stable ring to 'a later, separately stated step'; this is that step, as a Part II in the roadmap's own direction (RT-PAPER-BERGSTROM-FABER-PAYNE-24/7, as its verifier corrected it).
